groups.narrative: Over 20,000 industrial workers in Indonesia face potential layoffs due to currency depreciation and rising manufacturing operational costs.
groups.narrative_zh: 由于印尼盾持续贬值和原材料成本上升，印尼制造业面临超过2万名工人的裁员危机。

groups.R_reason: Based on official statistical reports of labor layoffs (PHK) compiled by the Ministry of Manpower.
groups.S_reason: Kemenaker is the official Indonesian government authority responsible for monitoring and publishing annual labor and layoff figures.
groups.T_reason: The resolution window will close when Kemenaker releases the cumulative 2026 figures, expected in early 2027.
groups.U_reason: High uncertainty due to fluctuating macroeconomic conditions, export market demand, and currency volatility in mid-2026.
groups.H_reason: Layoffs are a massive domestic political and social issue in Indonesia, covered extensively by local news outlets daily.

BDLT.B_reason: Highly relevant to local economic concerns, labor unions, and general public anxiety regarding job security.
BDLT.D_reason: Economic optimists expect a currency recovery to slow down layoffs, while pessimists point to structural industrial shifts.
BDLT.L_reason: Directly impacts the Indonesian workforce and domestic manufacturing hubs (West Java, Banten).
BDLT.T_reason: Will settle in early 2027 when cumulative annual figures are released.
